utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case IT-09-92-T, The Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, and good morning on my behalf as well. Mr. Lukic, I was informed that you would like to respond to the -- if I could say, the late 92 ter motions. There were three, one a little bit late, the other considerably late.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, if -- if I may. Your Honour, I thank you for this opportunity to address you on the three urgent motions filed by the Prosecution under Rule 92 ter. We on the Defence side have several concerns we must address. One, in addition to these three motions, we have other responses which are due within the next week. If we advance the day for these three we will be in a position of having full trial days and reviewing or drafting one or two responses a daily while we -- what we cannot do. Second, as to RM063 we have filed the response last night. For the other two, we cannot file expedited responses for these -- for the following reasons: RM165 and RM045, although filed Friday, were not served on the Defence until late yesterday morning. We have barely had a chance to look at them and both are lengthy. Third, RM165 was not even labelled as urgent by the Prosecution so we had no idea until yesterday's comments. It is impossible to call the witnesses next week when the Prosecution has just filed a motion seeking 61 associated exhibits and two statements for RM165 that we have not read yet. Respectfully, we have to insist on a regular 40-day briefing schedule. Four, as to the third motion, it too seeks two statements and part of a transcript to admit it and was filed much less than 30 days before the witness is scheduled to testify. That is not the fault of the Defence. We will try to get the responses done and filed by the end of this week. We are concerned that recently the Prosecution has started filing several motions as urgent that are entirely within their own control and which further strain the ability of the Defence to keep pace with what is needed to be done to keep up with trial. We are again at a point where every Prosecution filing almost seems to seek exception from the Rules, and we see it as unfair. And that's all we had on this topic, and thank you, Your Honours, for hearing me. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic. The Chamber will consider the matter. Mr. Groome would you like to respond at this moment or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Just briefly, Your Honour. I recognise that Mr. Lukic's position is not unreasonable. The Prosecution filed these motions on an urgent basis because of a gap that has opened up next week due in part because a witness, RM110, was advanced from that week to -- because the Defence took less time examining a witness and also because one of the witnesses scheduled, the Prosecution understood its obligations under Rule 68 to require an inquiry that we had to postpone that witness. I would just note for the Chamber that if the Chamber decides, and I think the Chamber would be reasonable in deciding that the motion should not be decided on an urgent basis, that there will be a gap next week of one, possibly two days, but we will inform the Chamber as soon as we have a clearer idea of where we stand. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And in anticipation of what the Chamber may do, could you see already whether there's any opportunity to use those days in a -- but that might result in more urgent motions, but there may be viva voce witnesses, there may be very technical witnesses for which not much preparation is needed. I wouldn't know. But ...

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I can assure the Chamber that we explored every option, and this was the last resort to file these motions urgently.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Then for the next witness, we move into closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. I have to inform the parties that since there are technical difficulties in Courtroom I, that we have to share this courtroom with another Trial Chamber, and we have tried to accommodate each other. Judges often have their own programmes during the time when we're not sitting, and for that reason, and, exceptionally, because we always try to accommodate Mr. Mladic as well in his wish to sit in the morning hours, that we would have to start tomorrow morning at 9.00 instead of 9.30, that we would then continue until a quarter to 2.00 instead of a quarter past 2.00. And for Thursday, the 15th of November, we would sit in the afternoon starting at 4.15 [sic] until 7.00 at night. Before we finally decide to do this, I would like to hear if there are any major objections by the parties on this new schedule. One second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When I said 4.15, I have meant 1415. That means quarter past 2.00 in the afternoon until 7.00. That is a full afternoon session. Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't believe so. But I will check with the witnesses after court and I shall inform by e-mail if there should be a problem.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We adjourn for the day, and we'll resume tomorrow morning, Wednesday, the 14th of November, at 9.00 in the morning in this same courtroom, III.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 14th day of November, 2012, at 9.00 a.m. 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.20 p.m.,
